finding.expected: Preserve legacy parse_tiktok_price behavior unchanged for search-card discovery, but make the strict exact-PDP price helper independently preserve an unambiguous explicit zero as 0.0 while continuing to reject negative, malformed, ranged, variant-dependent, multi-number, or conflicting price representations. Apply the same rule when the collector reconciles current_price and original_price. Add focused offline regressions showing exact-PDP price zero and original-price zero remain 0.0, missing prices remain None, ambiguous/ranged prices remain None, and existing search-card zero/range behavior remains unchanged. Do not broaden fields, live acquisition, browser ownership, Product Source, Affiliate, roadmap handoff, or any other TASK-232 authority.
finding.issue: TASK-232 explicitly requires strict exact-PDP scalar admission to preserve an explicitly observed zero wherever ProductCandidateSnapshot permits zero, with sold_count and review_count named as particular examples rather than the only fields. ProductCandidateSnapshot permits price and original_price values of 0.0, but parse_tiktok_pdp_price delegates its final scalar to legacy parse_tiktok_price, whose historical search-card contract rejects zero/non-positive prices. Consequently an exact PDP displaying an unambiguous scalar price of 0 is converted to None/unknown, collapsing OBSERVED_ZERO into MISSING. This directly violates AC3 and also prevents AC4 from being fully satisfied for an observed V1 price, while AC5 lacks regression proof for zero-valued current/original price.
